source_text: In uno homine iure vituperatur intentio et origo laudatur, quia duosunt, quae contrariis adplicentur; in parvulo autem unum est, natura tantum, quia voluntas non est. Illud ergo unum aut Deo adscribetur, aut daemoni. Si natura per Deum est, non potest in ea esse originale malum; si a diabolo, nihil erit, per quod homo divino operi vindicetur. Perfecte itaque Manichaeus est, qui malum originale defendit
pass_a_gloss: In one human being intention is rightly blamed and origin is praised, because there are two things which may be applied to contrary judgments; but in the little one there is one thing, nature only, because there is no will. That one thing therefore will be ascribed either to God or to a daemon. If nature is through God, original evil cannot be in it; if from the devil, there will be nothing through which the human being is claimed for the divine work. Perfectly therefore is he a Manichaean who defends original evil.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: In one person, the intention is rightly condemned and the origin praised, because there are two things to which opposite judgments can be applied. In an infant, however, there is only one thing: nature alone, because there is no will. That one thing, then, must be assigned either to God or to a demon. If nature comes through God, there can be no original evil in it. If it comes from the devil, there will be no basis for claiming the human being as God’s work. Thus anyone who defends original evil is thoroughly Manichaean.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
